sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Production and Global Distribution of Vertical Micro-Dramas

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) bilateral investment treaty with the United States (66 U.S.T. 399, entered into force 1966, terminated 2013)
BLEU Bilateral Investment Treaty with the People's Republic of China (signed 21 November 2005, entered into force 21 April 2009)
Luxembourg-Germany Double Taxation Agreement (DTA) of 23 August 2012 as amended by the 2020 protocol
Luxembourg-Netherlands DTA of 8 May 2012 (extension of the Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union duty point, as amended)
Luxembourg-United Kingdom DTA of 10 June 2019 (replacing 1967 treaty)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Consolidated Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended by the Law of 27 October 2010, the Law of 13 January 2019 (implementing EU Directive 2016/849, AMLD4), and the Law of 25 March 2020 on the establishment of the beneficial ownership register (RBE); supplemented by Grand-Ducal Regulation of 14 January 2019, CSSF Circular 20/729, and RCS registry guidance on UBO filing.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_verify_standard: Beneficial ownership comprises any natural person ultimately owning or controlling, directly or indirectly through a chain, 25% or more of the shares/voting rights or otherwise exercising ultimate control through ownership or other means; nominee holdings must be disregarded for UBO identification.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Articles of Association (Statuts) of the SARL, executed before a Luxembourg notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary (Notaire) appointed by the incorporators
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by Luxembourg notary; if a foreign power of attorney or corporate resolution is used, that item must be legalized via Hague Apostille (if originating in an Apostille Convention state) or via consular legalization at a Luxembourg embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of an identification document (passport or national ID) of each incorporator and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National authority of each natural person's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, plus notarized translation into official Luxembourg administrative language (French or German)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Utility bill or bank certificate evidencing residential address for each natural person (proof of address)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility supplier or financial institution in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; original must not be older than 3 months

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of non-registration (absence of prior corporate name) issued by the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) -- name reservation certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Direct issuance in Luxembourg; no further legalization when used within Luxembourg RCS process

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or proof of paid-up share capital deposit (minimum share capital €12,000 for SARL) issued by a regulated credit institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg or EU credit institution holding the capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by the issuing bank; no apostille required if issued by a Luxembourg or EU bank, otherwise Hague Apostille

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners against the CSSF consolidated lists, EU Council consolidated financial sanctions list, United Nations Security Council sanctions, and OFAC SDN List. PEPs and their family members/close associates are subject to enhanced due diligence, including source of wealth verification. The screening must be carried out at incorporation and continuously thereafter. Beneficial owners with PEP status require approval by senior management according to a written internal procedure.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.aml_suspicion_reporting_gateway: Direct submission of suspicious transaction reports to FIU Luxembourg (Cellule de Renseignement Financier, CRF) under Article 5 of the AML Law of 2004.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.notary_and_registered_agent_obligation: The Luxembourg notary is the obliged entity at filing; the RCS verifies beneficial ownership information and notifies the CSSF of discrepancies under the Law of 13 January 2019.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (www.lbr.lu) – electronic platform of the Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be expressed in French, German, or Luxembourgish; if the name is in a foreign language (e.g., English for the vertical micro-drama entity), a Luxembourg/foreign name transliteration is admitted provided it uses Latin characters and can be spelled in French or German. Names must not be misleading, must not infringe third-party rights, and must be clearly distinguishable in the RCS database. The RCS reserves the right to refuse names that cannot be transliterated or pronounced in an administrative language.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.name_rejection_grounds: Non-distinctiveness, conflict with existing registered enterprise names or trademarks, misleading representation of activity, or public policy concerns.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within one month of rejection by the RCS, the applicant may file an appeal with the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'Arrondissement) using an attorney-at-law (avocat). Simultaneously, a fresh name reservation can be requested, as no extension of the 30-day reservation is permitted. The RCS's decision can also be challenged by way of an administrative nullity action, but the direct judicial appeal before the commercial section (chambre commerciale) is the standard remedy.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office not accepted for a SARL carrying on television/motion picture production and distribution; the law requires a real, physical registered office (siège social) situated in Luxembourg at a precise address. A post-office box or virtual address is impermissible. The registered office must be a location where documents can be served and where corporate records are legally retained. For production operations, a separate operational address may exist, but the registered office must be a genuine administrative location.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate; unannounced inspections by RCS, CSSF (if applicable), and tax authorities are statistically unlikely for a low-risk media company, but the RCS and tax authorities may conduct onsite presence checks upon a complaint or a trigger event (e.g., UBO reporting discrepancies). The estimated probability for a fully compliant low-risk SARL in the first year is between 5% and 10%.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.commercial_substance_criteria: Maintain a Luxembourg bank account, keep minutes and records in Luxembourg, hold board meetings at the registered office, employ local administrative support or outsource to a licensed fiduciary, and ensure the actual management decisions are taken in Luxembourg.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notary public fee for execution of the articles of association (includes statutory drafting and legalization coordination)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary (notarial tariff law of 1960; market benchmark €1,200–€2,000)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff (Règlement du 21 mars 1960), variable on capital and ancillary services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS (Trade and Companies Register) registration fee for the SARL (immatriculation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Administrative tariff under Grand-Ducal Regulation of 25 March 1996, as amended

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS name reservation certificate (certificat de non-immatriculation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official fee schedule of the RCS (€25–€30)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal due diligence and drafting of ancillary documents (incorporation joinder, shareholders' agreement, directors minutes)
Apostille and legalization of foreign corporate documents (passports, bank references, powers of attorney)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the origin country and/or Consulate of Luxembourg abroad
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular fee schedules and Hague Apostille fees, per document (approx. €10–€50 per document plus courier)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO registration filing (opening of RBE file and submission of beneficial owner data)
Registered office physical address service for one fiscal year (including board meeting room access and mail handling)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed fiduciary or real estate provider in Luxembourg-City

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate seals, statutory registers, digital vault, and translation of formation documents into administrative language
Contingency buffer for ministerial approvals or supplementary legalization of sensitive name tokens (if applicable)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Expected fixed government tax or notary fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as amended; SARL regime under Articles 442-1 to 466; notarized incorporation deed required under Article 5; legal personality conferred upon RCS registration under Article 10; filing and publication with the Luxembourg Business Registers under Article 90.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), attached to the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg; electronic filings made via the eJuste platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized deed of incorporation (Acte constitutif containing the Statuts), filed electronically with the RCS and published in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed capital is EUR 12,000. The full capital must be subscribed as cash or in-kind; each share must be paid up to at least 25% of its nominal value, with cash contributions (minimum EUR 3,000) deposited in a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) at a Luxembourg credit institution and evidenced by a banker's blocking certificate; contributions in kind must be fully transferred at incorporation and valued by a statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF LU_SARL (Société à Responsabilité Limitée): The founders and first director resolve by unanimous written consent: 1. Share Subscription: the issued capital of EUR 12,000 is fully subscribed and deposited in a blocked escrow account at a Luxembourg credit institution; shares are allotted and the release order is approved. 2. Registered Office: the registered office is fixed at [address], Luxembourg, as the official seat for legal service. 3. Officers: [Name] is appointed sole manager (Gérant) with singular signature authority. 4. The manager is authorised to complete RCS filing, VAT registration, and ancillary procedures. Unanimously adopted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Corporate Name Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS online name search at lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a real-time conflict search on the LBR and RESA databases for identical or confusingly similar corporate names; verify protected surnames and trademarks; reserve the chosen distinctive name or obtain a name-clearance confirmation to annex to the notarized deed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit an amended reservation bearing a new distinctive element; re-run the online search and present the fresh clearance certificate to the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Capital Escrow Account and Banker's Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (e.g., BNP Paribas Luxembourg, Spuerkeess/BCEE) in the name of the future SARL
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary escrow account in the name of the future SARL; deposit the minimum paid-up cash amount (at least 25% of EUR 12,000 = EUR 3,000); instruct the bank to issue a blocking certificate (attestation de blocage de fonds) naming the notary as beneficiary, to be released only upon production of the RCS registration extract.
required_dossiers: Bank onboarding and anti-money laundering forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Remediate KYC gaps by submitting certified identity and source-of-funds documents; designate a Luxembourg resident to complete bank interviews; transfer funds from another Luxembourg-resident account to accelerate clearance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Notaire luxembourgeois; list via Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the chosen notary with all incorporators or their powers of attorney; sign the notarial act containing the statuts, the subscription schedule, and the irrevocable powers of the first manager; the notary verifies the escrow certificate, legality, capital rules, and the absence of disqualifications, then delivers certified copies for RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Valuation report of the statutory auditor for in-kind contributions (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The notary serves an observation note (remarque) requiring clause amendments; revise the statuts, reconvene a second signing session, and re-execute a rectified notarial deed within the cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration, Legal Personality, and Publication in RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS via the eJuste electronic filing portal of the Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the certified notarial deed, the e-form signed by the manager, and the statutory annexes through eJuste; pay the registration fee; obtain the RCS corporate number; legal personality and corporate existence result from this registration; publication is effectuated in the RESA legal gazette on the same file.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarized deed
Identification and residence evidence of the manager
Declaration of domiciliation or lease of the registered office
Proof of payment of filing fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the file, correct discrepancies via an eJuste amendment submission, pay the applicable cure fee, and re-file; a formal refusal may be appealed to the District Court of Luxembourg within the statutory delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Formation Tax, VAT, Social Security, and Operational Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Administration de l'enregistrement et des domaines (AED); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS); Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SARL for corporate income tax and municipal business tax with ACD, obtain a Luxembourg VAT number (numéro de TVA) from AED, register as employer with CCSS, and comply with ITM workplace-declaration obligations; procure the corporate seal, open the operational bank account, and establish the statutory share register and minutes book.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarial deed
Identity documents of the managing director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late-registration penalty notices may be challenged by filing proof of the RCS date; voluntary correction (régularisation spontanée) and the zero-interest payment plan with ACD and AED cure procedural defaults.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 5911 digital short-drama production and OTT distribution; no industrial establishment (établissement classé) authorization required. If a physical recording studio is later added, the competent authority is the Ministry of the Economy – Direction générale de l'industrie (commodo/incommodo procedure under the Law of 14 March 2017).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no operational manufacturing permit for a short-drama streaming platform; optional incentive-based registration with Film Fund Luxembourg (Fonds national de soutien à la production audiovisuelle) for co-production subsidies only.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – pure digital services with no listed installations trigger no EIA; registration-tier only if office premises exceed the commodo/incommodo comfort thresholds. No Full EIA Report is required for vertical micro-drama streaming activities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or waste-handling emission ceilings are triggered for app-based production; indirect compliance applies to EU WEEE and RoHS regimes for streaming hardware, the EU Code of Conduct for Data Centres energy efficiency, GDPR data-protection obligations for platform content, and, if a studio is later used, the EU Industrial Emissions Directive 2010/75/EU thresholds remain below permitting limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (attestation de sécurité incendie) from the Administration des services de secours (CGDISS) for the registered office and any studio; structural load certificate for office occupancy; occupational clearance from ITM covering ergonomic workstations, electrical installations, emergency exits, and the submission of the labor regulations (règlement intérieur); no special civil-defense clearance is required for streaming platforms.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) - Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (https://impotsdirects.public.lu); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) - Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Authority (https://pfi.public.lu); Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (LBR/RCS, https://www.lbr.lu); unified e-government portal: MyGuichet.lu (https://guichet.public.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the SARL by notarial deed; the notary registers the company with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS), obtaining the 11-digit business registration number (matricule) and, if required, the national EORI number. Step 2: Upon RCS registration, the AEDT issues the Luxembourg VAT identification number (numéro de TVA) ex officio for taxable companies; the SARL confirms activity details via Form 640 submitted electronically through MyGuichet.lu or the AEDT eCDF portal. Step 3: The ACD issues the corporate income tax NIF (numéro d'identification fiscale) for income tax and municipal business tax purposes; the SARL registers for impôt commercial communal (ICC) with the commune of its registered seat. Step 4 (non-resident suppliers): A foreign entity without a Luxembourg establishment that makes taxable supplies in Luxembourg must register directly with the AEDT (Form 640A for EU-established taxable persons); non-EU entities must appoint an approved Luxembourg tax representative (Article 63 of the Luxembourg VAT Law) unless the OSS/IOSS or reverse-charge mechanism applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; territorial_scope = resident company subject to worldwide taxation with participation exemption (Art. 166 LIR); pass_through = not eligible, classical corporate tax system; tax_exempt_zone = not applicable. A Luxembourg SARL is a fully taxable resident capital company: corporate income tax 15% plus 7% solidarity surcharge (16.05% base), municipal business tax (ICC) 6.75%-11.5%, and net wealth tax 0.5%; aggregate effective rate in Luxembourg City approximately 24.94%.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists under Luxembourg law; classification is statutory. Available elections and regimes: (1) Fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) under Art. 164bis LIR for resident subsidiaries at least 95% owned by a Luxembourg resident company; (2) Participation exemption (Art. 166 LIR) for dividends and capital gains from qualifying shareholdings of at least 10% or EUR 1.2 million acquisition cost held at least 12 months; (3) VAT grouping (assujetti unique) under Art. 60 of the Luxembourg VAT Law; (4) Option to subject real estate leases to VAT under Art. 43 of the VAT Law (not relevant to digital micro-drama streaming); (5) ATAD/ATAD2 hybrid mismatch rules (Law of 21 June 2019) apply automatically without elective relief; (6) Audiovisual investment tax credit of 30-35% of qualifying production expenditure for ISIC 5911 production activities, subject to prior approval by the Luxembourg Film Fund.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA) - Luxembourg value added tax under the Loi du 12 février 1979 relative à la TVA, as amended, harmonized with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (excluding VAT) for the small-business exemption (franchise) under Art. 57 of the VAT Law. Non-established foreign suppliers have no registration threshold and must register when making taxable supplies in Luxembourg unless reverse charge applies. For intra-EU distance sales of electronic services to B2C consumers, the EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold (Art. 57bis VAT Law) determines whether Luxembourg VAT applies; digital streaming sales to non-EU consumers fall outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control API mandate exists in Luxembourg. E-invoicing is permitted (EN 16931 for B2G under Directive 2014/55/EU) but B2B e-invoicing is not mandated. Electronic VAT return filing is mandatory for SARLs via the AEDT eCDF portal with monthly, quarterly, or annual frequency based on turnover. Payment service providers (Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, Stripe) must report cross-border payments under the EU CESOP framework (Regulation 2020/283) quarterly to the ACD/AEDT. SAF-T format is used for tax audit data exchange without pre-clearance. The OSS/IOSS portals are used to declare B2C digital services and distance sales of goods.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT (exonération avec droit à déduction) applies to: (1) export of goods outside the EU (Art. 39 VAT Law / Art. 146 EU VAT Directive) with proof of physical exit from EU customs territory; (2) intra-Community supplies of goods to a B2B customer holding a valid EU VAT identification number (Art. 38 VAT Law / Art. 138 EU VAT Directive); (3) services directly related to exports and international transport (Arts. 40-42 VAT Law). For the vertical micro-drama streaming business: streaming and digital downloads sold B2C to non-EU consumers are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT (place of supply is the customer's residence under Art. 58 VAT Law); B2B licensing of intellectual and economic rights in micro-drama content to non-EU licensees qualifies as zero-rated/outside scope where the recipient is established outside the EU (Art. 14(1)(11°) VAT Law), preserving full input VAT deduction. Substantiation requires evidence of the customer's status as a taxable person, country of establishment, and actual exploitation of the rights.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/EAD lodged in the Luxembourg PLDA customs system, including EORI number and customs office exit confirmation)
Bill of Lading, CMR Road Consignment Note, or Airway Bill evidencing physical departure of goods from EU customs territory

Inward Remittance Certificate or bank payment records evidencing receipt of proceeds in convertible currency (for global distribution licensing: the license agreement, royalty statements, and remittance records)
Commercial invoices with packing list, and for intra-EU B2B supplies: the customer's valid VAT identification number and the recapitulative statement (EC Sales List)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may retrospectively assess Luxembourg VAT at 17% plus late interest of 0.8% per month where export substantiation is deficient. Under Art. 53 of the VAT Law and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 30 December 1991, proof of export/intra-community supply must be completed within 3 months of the transaction and retained for 10 years. Administrative fines under Arts. 61-62 of the VAT Law range from EUR 250 to EUR 4,000 for non-compliance. VAT fraud, including false export declarations, sham licensing structures, or circular transactions aimed at obtaining zero-rating or input VAT refunds, is punishable by imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years and/or fines of EUR 4,000 to EUR 250,000, with a 10-year limitation period for fraudulent assessment and a 5-year period in non-fraud cases. The AEDT coordinates with OLAF and foreign tax administrations under EU mutual assistance and DAC Directives. Transfer-pricing documentation and economic substance evidence must substantiate the royalty and IP licensing arrangements on audit; the Luxembourg IP box (80% exemption) and net wealth tax filings are separately scrutinized.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting under the European System of Central Banks (ESCB); monetary and foreign exchange policy authority is the European Central Bank (ECB) for the euro area. Banking and payment licensing supervision rests with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. Luxembourg imposes no exchange controls, no prior authorisation requirements for capital movements, and no restrictions on dividend, interest, royalty, or profit remittances. Free movement of capital and payments is guaranteed by Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU). Non-resident ownership of a Luxembourg SARL is permitted and capital inflows and outflows may be made freely in any currency. Only standard corporate income tax, municipal business tax, net wealth tax, and any treaty-based withholding taxes apply on repatriated profits, and no separate FX or central bank clearance is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Luxembourg and the euro area do not impose mandatory surrender, conversion, or repatriation timelines for export proceeds. Foreign currency receivables may be retained, converted, or transferred freely.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. A fintech electronic money institution (EMI) authorised in another EEA state may provide local euro IBANs, SEPA payments, and currency conversion facilities in Luxembourg through the PSD2 passporting regime without a separate Luxembourg banking licence. Legal constraints include prohibition on lending or credit services, safeguarding requirements for client funds, limited access to SWIFT correspondent banking, and potentially enhanced due diligence when handling high-volume app-store receipts. An EMI is viable as a secondary operational or collection rail, but a full-service Luxembourg credit institution is recommended for capital escrow, treasury management, and large trade settlements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is generally permissible for non-resident directors and shareholders using video identification and qualified electronic signatures in accordance with CSSF Circular 20/744 and eIDAS Regulation (EU) No 910/2014. Certain banks may nevertheless require a physical interview where the ultimate beneficial owner resides in a non-EEA or high-risk jurisdiction, where the corporate structure involves opacity, or where sanctions screening flags unusual patterns. The physical appearance mandate is bank-specific and may be waived on the basis of a compliant remote on-boarding dossier.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO structure with intermediate holding vehicles in multiple jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified group structure chart showing the chain of ownership to natural-person UBOs; certified articles of association of every holding entity; share register and board resolutions; Luxembourg UBO register extract under the law of 13 January 2019; equivalent beneficial ownership filings for all non-resident intermediate vehicles; commercial substance evidence for each entity; a business plan explaining the group's operating and financing strategy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intragroup cross-border transactions involving production services, IP licensing, distribution fees, and streaming royalties under vertical micro-drama model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed intercompany agreements covering IP ownership, cost-sharing, distribution, production services, and streaming platform arrangements; OECD-compliant transfer pricing documentation with an economic analysis; audited or management financial statements of the Luxembourg entity and key foreign counterparts; evidence of local substance, including staff, office presence, executive decisions, and actual commercial activities; any applicable tax ruling or advance pricing agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, geographically dispersed micro-payments from Apple App Store, Google Play, and card-processing platforms with substantial customer refunds and chargeback exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: App store settlement statements for a trailing six-to-twelve month period; executed merchant agreements with Apple, Google, and Stripe; payment processor transaction logs and reconciliation reports; customer refund and chargeback policy; AML transaction monitoring and sanctions screening procedures; description of automated treasury reconciliation, fraud controls, and an independent audit of payment data if available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder capital injections by debt financing or share premium from a wholly foreign parent without clear source of wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank confirmation of the origin of funds supported by SWIFT MT103 or MT202 messages; source-of-wealth file including audited financial statements, tax returns, bank reference, or sale agreements; formal capital contribution or shareholder loan agreements; board resolutions approving the injection; notarised corporate documents; auditor confirmation and guarantee of beneficial-ownership transparency.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound euro capital contributions are routed via the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) or standard SWIFT transfers; cross-currency contributions use the SWIFT network with ISO 20022 transaction purpose code EQUI (equity capital) or the Combined Nomenclature purpose classification for direct investments. Verification requires the corporate subscription resolutions, notarised board minutes, share register updates, UBO declarations, and confirmation of the originating bank for source-of-funds screening. Customer funds are released to the operational account only after satisfactory AML/KYC checks and, where relevant, the declaration of exceptional cash payments.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for production vendor services, distribution licences, and streaming software expenses are executed via SWIFT MT103 for single direct payments, MT202 COV for correspondent bank cover, and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for low-value intra-EEA disbursements. Large contractual disbursements to production suppliers may be structured as commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700) at sight or with deferred payment terms, supported by conforming shipping or delivery documentation; documentary collections (SWIFT MT400/MT540) are used where security of exchange is required but without full letter-of-credit formality. Every disbursement is reconciled against the underlying contract, purchase order, or licence agreement and logged against corporate tax and transfer pricing records.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards on EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CNY for committed revenue and cost flows
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with restricted deliverability referenced in streaming-market settlement
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) to transform USD-denominated app-store revenues into EUR treasury obligations
Vanilla FX options (purchased put and call options) on EUR/USD for defensive hedging without upside limitation
FX swaps combining a spot trade with a matched forward transaction for temporary liquidity coverage

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements filing (comptes annuels) with the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after close of financial year (normally 30 June for calendar-year SARL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fines up to EUR 5,000; continuous non-compliance may lead to judicial dissolution or administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (déclaration de l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (ACD - Administration des contributions directes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing due 30 June of the following year for calendar-year taxpayers (extendable to 31 December without penalty)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default surcharge of 0.6% of reported taxes per month; late filing penalty of up to EUR 30,000 plus 10% of assessed tax

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual net wealth tax return (déclaration de l'impôt sur la fortune)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as corporate income tax return (30 June next year, extendable to 31 December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of EUR 25 to EUR 1,000 per month of delay; interest at 0.6% per month on unpaid net wealth tax

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return (déclaration annuelle de TVA) and annual listing of transactions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: VAT annual return due 31 March following the calendar year; annual transaction listing due 31 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fine up to EUR 20,000; late payment interest at 1% per month plus 10% penalty

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO confirmation filing (confirmation annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS - Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after the anniversary of the initial registration date of the entity (calendar-year rule)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 for directors; administrative strike-off possible for persistent default

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit required if SARL exceeds two of three cumulative limits: total balance sheet > EUR 4.4 million, net turnover > EUR 8.8 million, average 50 employees; micro-entities below thresholds are exempt unless shareholders holding 10% or more request audit
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Luxembourg legal chart of accounts) in accordance with the Luxembourg law of 19 December 2002; IFRS optional for statutory accounts if listed or cross-border groups

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: SARL must file an annual confirmation with the RCS (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) confirming the identity and ownership percentage of each beneficial owner; any share transfer during the year must be reported within 1 month of the transfer; failure to update triggers criminal sanctions against directors

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - USD 2,500 per year for registered office and corporate agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 15,000 per year for mandatory audit (if thresholds exceeded); not applicable for micro-SARL below audit thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 18.19% (17% corporate income tax plus 7% solidarity surcharge; excludes municipal business tax of approximately 6.75% in Luxembourg City, bringing the aggregate effective headcount to approximately 24.94% for a Luxembourg City operation)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 80% exemption for qualifying intellectual property income (IP box regime, producing an effective rate around 4.5%); investment tax credit of 8% (ordinary) to 12% for digital and 3D animation assets; notional interest deduction on new contributing share capital and share premium

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Luxembourg corporate income tax return: Form 100 (FNR 100) filed electronically via the MyGuichet.lu professional e-Space; also available via the Luxembourg direct tax administration's eCDF platform for supplementary schedules
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year taxpayer, the return and financial statements must be filed by 31 May following the tax year; extended deadlines of up to 12 months may be granted on prior written application to the relevant Bureau d'imposition

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: legal name, legal form, RCS number (Business Register), address of registered office, Luxembourg tax identification number (numéro de dossier)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SARL deriving Luxembourg-source income from a permanent establishment or immovable property must insert its local tax number and the name and address of its appointed Luxembourg tax representative; a foreign NIFE number must be converted into a Luxembourg local dossier number

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax period and business activity: opening and closing dates of the accounting year; exact NACE / ISIC code (5911 for motion picture production; NAICS 512110 for video production)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only the Luxembourg permanent establishment's accounting period and the activities actually attributable to that establishment; do not report worldwide activity in the local return

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating results and taxable income reconciliation: commercial net profit per the statutory financial statements, adjusted with non-deductible expenses, tax-exempt income, investment credits, IP box deductions, loss carryforward utilisation, and arm's-length transfer pricing adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must file a branch-specific income statement limited to Luxembourg-sourced gross revenue and deductible branch expenses; allocations must follow the OECD Permanent Establishment profit attribution principles under Article 7 of the Luxembourg treaty network

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transactions and transfer pricing schedule: identification of counterparties, countries, amounts, and applied arm's length method
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare all intercompany revenue and costs booked through the Luxembourg entity or branch, including short-drama licensing, app store monetisation, and sub-licensing of content IP to or from foreign group companies

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Effective shareholding and capital structure: beneficial ownership schedule, shareholding percentage, date of acquisition, and declaration of dividend distribution intentions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Used for applying the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption or treaty dividend relief; attach the certificate of tax residence of the ultimate parent and evidence of the 12-month holding period

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing is sanctioned by a fiscal penalty of up to 10% of the total tax assessed, plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.5% per month on the unpaid tax; repeated non-filing can trigger a tax assessment by administrative estimation under the Luxembourg General Tax Law (AO §217) and a non-deductibility of penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain a reduced rate or exemption, the beneficial owner must lodge a written relief application with the Luxembourg direct tax administration in the year of distribution, enclosing an original certificate of tax residence (TRC) issued by its home jurisdiction, evidence of the minimum shareholding percentage and, where applicable, evidence of the uninterrupted 12-month holding period. For EU-resident parent companies holding at least 10% of the SARL for 12 months, the exemption is applied at source under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive without prior refund; treaty-only relief normally requires submission of a withholding tax refund request on Form 100, Annex 1, to the Bureau d'imposition once the tax has been remitted.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Luxembourg withholding tax on outbound royalties and interest is generally 0% for non-residents, provided that the payments are not economically connected with a Luxembourg permanent establishment and are made at arm's length. Interest paid to controlling shareholders under profit-participating loans or convertible debt may be reclassified as constructive dividends and exposed to the 15% dividend WHT. Securities debt interest paid to a Luxembourg corporate payer is also subject to the same 15% WHT where the lender qualifies as a related party under the domestic rules, unless treaty relief applies.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 100,000 in aggregate for cross-border controlled transactions of the same category during the tax year; Luxembourg does not impose a separate statutory local-file threshold for small operators, but the tax administration may require full OECD-aligned TP documentation when this threshold is exceeded. For groups with consolidated revenue of EUR 750 million or more, a CbC report must be filed with the Luxembourg tax authorities via the Ministry of Finance.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies Economic Substance principles through general anti-abuse rules (the ATAD GAAR, implemented by Article 6 of the Law on Tax Procedure) and through the Principal Purpose Test (PPT) under the MLI. A SARL producing and distributing vertical micro-dramas must demonstrate sufficient local substance: real operational management in Luxembourg, qualified employees engaged in production, licensing, or distribution activities, independent decision-making for acquisition and monetisation of film rights, actual office space, and bank accounts. A conduit that merely interposes Luxembourg between third-party video platforms and foreign production companies without operational substance will be disregarded, and income will be requalified in the hands of the foreign principal.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission or misstatement of taxable Luxembourg-source revenue from short-drama app monetisation, including concealed Apple IAP and Google Play Billing receipts, fictitious licence deductions, or non-declared related-party distributions to shareholders
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines from EUR 10,000 to EUR 50,000 plus 10% increase of the evaded tax and late interest of 0.5% per month; criminal prosecution under Luxembourg General Tax Law (AO §§395–400) may impose imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years for deliberate false declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false tax returns, authorise artificial transfer pricing markups, or direct the diversion of streaming revenue are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt; travel bans and provisional detention may be ordered, and convicted directors face disqualification from managing Luxembourg legal entities under the commercial code.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Luxembourg SARL as a pure letterbox entity with no personnel, no premises, no management activity, and no economic substance, while channelling short-drama streaming royalties through Luxembourg solely to exploit the participation exemption or a favourable treaty
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation of the entire arrangement under the GAAR and the MLI Principal Purpose Test; denial of treaty benefits; reclassification of intercompany licensing revenue as taxable Luxembourg income; imposition of 15% dividend WHT on constructive distributions; plus an administrative penalty of 50% of the recharacterised tax benefit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who act as nominal managers for a shell arrangement may be personally assessed for the shortfall, face forced removal of the company from the Luxembourg trade register, and be criminally liable for fraud against creditors; travel restrictions under the Luxembourg tax collection procedure are also available against directors of disregarded shell companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure by the Luxembourg SARL to identify and verify beneficial owners of intellectual property licensing revenues, use of anonymous e-wallet payment rails, concealment of the ultimate economic owner of the streaming app, or execution of licence payments to sanctioned persons without conducting a sanctions-predicate check
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adminstrative fine of up to EUR 5 million or 10% of annual turnover under the Law of 12 November 2004 (AMLD4/5 implementation), plus asset freezing by the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit; the company may be prohibited from continuing the payment rails and bank accounts may be closed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly omit UBO information, sign false AML declarations, or authorise payments to a blacklisted party face personal fines up to EUR 500,000, imprisonment up to 5 years, and civil restitution for any deception-induced losses; the corporate veil is pierced where the SARL serves as a Cuir-Lux instrument in a fraudulent international scheme.
